skill.name: webapp-testing
skill.description: Toolkit for interacting with and testing local web applications using Playwright. Supports verifying frontend functionality, debugging UI behavior, capturing browser screenshots, and viewing browser logs.
skill.summary: Test local web applications with Playwright, managed development servers, screenshots, element discovery, and browser console capture.
skill.author: ArtemisAI

security_audit.summary: Two subprocess findings are confirmed because caller-controlled values can launch arbitrary processes, including a server command through a shell. The remaining 28 findings are safe local URLs, expected artifact writes, or Markdown backticks, but the instruction to execute scripts before inspection is a separate high-risk prompt injection concern.

remediation.issue: The server helper passes a caller-controlled command to subprocess.Popen with shell=True.
remediation.suggestion: Accept an argument vector instead of a shell string, remove shell=True, and require explicit approval for every server command.

remediation.issue: The helper directly executes the caller-provided test command.
remediation.suggestion: Show the resolved command, require explicit approval, validate executable and script paths, and run within a restricted project environment.

remediation.issue: The skill tells agents to run bundled scripts before reading their source and to treat them as black boxes.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the anti-inspection guidance and require source, dependency, and command review before any bundled script is executed.

content.user_title: Test Local Web Applications with Playwright
content.value_statement: Local interface failures can be difficult to reproduce and diagnose. This skill guides Playwright checks, server management, screenshots, element discovery, and console capture.
actual_capabilities: Starts one or more local development servers and waits for their ports before running a test command.
Guides synchronous Python Playwright scripts for local dynamic applications and static HTML files.
Discovers visible buttons, links, and form fields to support selector selection.
Captures full-page screenshots before or after browser interactions.
Collects browser console messages and saves them as a local testing artifact.
limitations: Python, Playwright, browser binaries, and application dependencies must already be installed.
The server helper can execute arbitrary commands and requires command review and explicit approval.
Examples use fixed local paths and URLs that must be adapted to the current environment.
The examples do not provide assertions, authentication handling, or a complete regression test framework.

use_cases.title: Verify a Local Interface
use_cases.description: Frontend engineers can verify navigation, forms, and rendered states while developing a local application.

use_cases.title: Investigate Browser Failures
use_cases.description: Quality engineers can discover selectors, capture screenshots, and collect console output before writing durable browser tests.

use_cases.title: Run Agent-Assisted Checks
use_cases.description: AI coding agents can start local services and run focused Playwright checks after explicit command review.

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Local Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the local application at {url}. Wait for network idle, capture a full-page screenshot, and report visible errors without changing data.

prompt_templates.title: Discover Stable Selectors
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect {url} and list visible buttons, links, and form fields. Recommend stable Playwright selectors for the workflow named {workflow}.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose an Interaction
prompt_templates.prompt: Reproduce {workflow} at {url}. Capture console errors and screenshots around each action, then report the first failing step and supporting evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Servers and Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Start {server_command} on port {port}. After I approve the resolved command, run {test_command} and summarize failures, console errors, and screenshots.

output_examples.input: Check the dashboard at localhost:5173 for visible errors.
output: No browser console errors were observed.
A full-page screenshot was saved for review.

output_examples.input: Discover interactive elements on the local sign-in page.
output: Two visible inputs were found: email and password.
One visible submit button was found with the label Sign in.
Role and label selectors are recommended for these controls.

output_examples.input: Investigate why the profile form does not submit.
output: The form accepted input, but submission produced a browser console error.
The first reproducible failure occurred after selecting Save.
Screenshots before and after submission were captured for comparison.

best_practices: Review and approve every server and test command before execution.
Wait for an appropriate load state before inspecting a dynamic page.
Prefer role, label, ID, or stable test selectors over fragile visual positions.
anti_patterns: Do not execute bundled scripts as black boxes without inspecting their source and dependencies.
Do not run browser automation against systems without authorization.
Do not rely only on fixed delays when a deterministic page or element state is available.

faq.question: Does this skill install Playwright?
faq.answer: No. Python, Playwright, supported browser binaries, and application dependencies must already be available.

faq.question: Can it start multiple local servers?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper accepts repeated server and port options, but each resolved command requires review and approval.

faq.question: Can it test static HTML files?
faq.answer: Yes. An included example opens a local HTML file through a file URL and performs browser interactions.

faq.question: Where are screenshots and logs stored?
faq.answer: The examples use fixed temporary or output directories. Adapt those paths to the current environment before running them.

faq.question: Can it test remote websites?
faq.answer: It is designed for local applications. Use remote targets only with authorization and after reviewing network and data handling requirements.

faq.question: Does it replace a complete test suite?
faq.answer: No. It supports focused inspection and debugging, but it does not provide comprehensive assertions, fixtures, coverage, or continuous integration.
